correctness.rationale: The barycentric orbit-realization lemma identifies fixed geometric points with admissible coset barycenters, with all positive support coefficients orbit-constant. For H of rank k, coordinate functional double counting yields s 2^(k-1)=sum_h wt(h)<=2(2^k-1), so s<=3; k=3 forces the full 3-cube and a weight-three codeword, contradiction, ruling out all k>=3. Rank-two distinct cosets would span a forbidden rank-three space if compatible, hence the orbit complex is discrete of the stated size. Rank-one weight-one cosets give the (n-1)-cube; weight-two cosets indexed by (p,y) give opposite parity adjacency at d(y,z)<=1 and the parity relabeling (p,y)->(p+sum y,y) gives exactly Q_(n-1), with no triangles/higher faces. Independent enumeration generated all binary subspaces for n=3..5 and verified each eligible orbit graph against the cube or isolated points (rank-one cases 6,10,15; rank-two cases 4,10,20). This corroborates but is not the infinite proof. Boundaries n=3 and empty fixed complexes addressed.

final_claim: For every n>=3 and nonzero binary translation subgroup H of (F_2)^n, the actual PL fixed locus of the inclusive Hamming-distance-2 Vietoris--Rips complex is Q_(n-1) if dim H=1 and max codeword weight<=2; is 2^(n-2) discrete points if dim H=2 and max weight<=2; and otherwise empty. The cube-graph Betti_1 is (n-3)2^(n-2)+1.
limitations: Only nonzero pure translation subgroups, n>=3, inclusive Hamming scale 2.
